newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cigarette business boosts Shanghai Ind profits.
newsitem.headline: Cigarette business boosts Shanghai Ind profits.

text.p: Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd on Thursday attributed its strong net earnings of HK$360 million to its outstanding cigarette business.
"The performance of the company's cigarettes business was outstanding," it said in a statement.
"The pro forma combined turnover for 1996 amounted to HK$1,096 million and pro forma combined operating profits HK$327 million," the statement said.
The 1996-incorporated company announced its first annual results for the year ended December 31, 1996, on Thursday.
Turnover stood at HK$1,317 million while earnings per share was HK$0.75, it said.
Its unit Nanyang Tobacco improved product mix, developed new products, strengthened cost controls and developed potential markets in southeast Asia during the year, the company said.
The company also intended to study plans to expand and improve production equipment and warehousing facilities.
As for its packaging and printing material business, pro forma combined turnover and operating profit for 1996 amounted to HK$202 million and HK$44 million, respectively.
In 1996, its Wing Fat Printing unit set up joint ventures in China, including Shaanxi and Zhejiang provinces.

On its cosmetic business, which yielded operating profits of HK$55 million, the company said it was beginning to enjoy growing customer loyalty, which led it to develop a new line of natural products incorporating Chinese herbal ingredients.
The company's pharmaceutical business yielded pro forma operating profit of HK$31 million.
